mission.display_title: Construct a confidence interval using a given sampling distribution
mission.mission_purpose: Today's Mission exists to construct a confidence interval for an unknown parameter using a given sampling distribution — so the given-distribution route is usable — without pretending Normal mean/variance recipes (3.2.4) are finished.
mission.tutor_intent: Today I will force the candidate to use a stated sampling distribution to form a CI and refuse treating Normal mean/variance cookbook as today's LO.

mission.learning_objective: Confidence interval for an unknown parameter using a given sampling distribution.
mission.concept_focus: Given sampling distribution → invert / pivot → CI → refuse Normal cookbook-as-done.
mission.prior_bridge: Yesterday you constructed a prediction interval (3.2.2). Today continues topic 3.2 at LO 3.2.3 — CI using a given sampling distribution.
mission.why_now: 3.2.3 is contiguous after prediction. Closing it prevents a cliff at the given-distribution method while keeping Normal mean/variance CIs as day four.
mission.expected_benefit: You will be able to form a CI by inverting a given sampling distribution, not only by recalling Normal-mean formulae.
mission.explainability: Assigned as Campaign Lambda Day 3 because Continuity Front membership places given-sampling-distribution CI after prediction.

knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Skipping the LO hinge or swallowing the next LO.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 3.2.3
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. For an Exponential mean-θ model you are told that 2n X̄ / θ ~ χ²_{2n}. (1) Outline how you invert this sampling distribution to form a CI for θ. (2) Refuse: 'I memorised the Normal-mean CI cookbook, so any sampling-distribution CI is done.'
knowledge_checks.body: Invert a given sampling distribution to form a CI; refuse Normal-cookbook-as-done.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Given-distribution CIs rearrange a known pivotal/sampling relationship; memorised Normal-mean recipes are not a substitute.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: (1) Choose χ² critical values so P(χ²_L < 2n X̄ / θ < χ²_U) = 1−α, then rearrange the inequality to isolate θ (bounds involve 2n X̄ / χ²). (2) Refuse: cookbook Normal-mean formulae do not replace inverting the given sampling distribution for this model.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Jumping to a Normal-mean CI template without using the given sampling distribution.
success_criteria: Outlines inversion/rearrangement of the given χ² relationship for θ.
Refuses treating Normal-mean cookbook as finishing this LO.
